q: What is the youngest age at which you can get a South Carolina beginner's permit?
exp: You must be at least 15 and pass the vision and knowledge tests to get a beginner's permit.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-4; S.C. Code § 56-1-50 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: With a beginner's permit, during which hours may you drive with a licensed driver who is 21 or older?
exp: From 6 a.m. to midnight you may drive with a qualified licensed driver 21 or older beside you; after midnight, only a qualified supervisor may ride with you.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-4; S.C. Code § 56-1-50 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: Who may supervise a permit driver between 6 a.m. and midnight?
a: A licensed driver 18 or older with at least one year of driving experience
b: A licensed driver 21 or older with at least three years of driving experience
c: A licensed driver 21 or older with at least one year of driving experience, in the front seat
d: Only a parent or legal guardian
exp: The supervisor must be at least 21, hold a license, have at least one year of driving experience and sit in the front seat.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-4; SCDMV, Beginner's Permits (dmv.sc.gov/Driver-Services/Drivers-License/Beginner-Permits)

q: If you are 17 or younger, how long must you hold your beginner's permit before you apply for a license?
exp: Drivers 17 and under hold the permit at least 180 days and may apply on day 181.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, pp. 1-4 to 1-5; S.C. Code § 56-1-50 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How long must a first-time driver who is 18 or older hold a beginner's permit before the road test?
exp: At 18 or older, you may apply for your license after holding the permit 30 days, on day 31.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-5; S.C. Code § 56-1-50 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How much supervised practice must a 15 or 16-year-old log before a first license?
exp: Teens applying at 15 or 16 practice at least 40 hours, with 10 hours of night driving, with a qualified supervisor.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, pp. 1-5 to 1-6; SCDMV, Teenage Drivers (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/teenage-drivers)

q: What driver education must a 15 or 16-year-old complete before a first license?
a: 30 hours in a classroom and 6 hours of driving
b: 8 hours in a classroom and 8 hours of driving
c: 8 hours in a classroom and 6 hours of driving
d: 24 hours in a classroom and 8 hours of driving
exp: The required course has 8 hours of classroom work and 6 hours behind the wheel.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-6; SCDMV, Teenage Drivers (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/teenage-drivers)

q: Outside daylight saving time, when may a conditional license holder drive alone?
exp: Conditional and special restricted license holders may drive alone from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., or until 8 p.m. during daylight saving time.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-7; S.C. Code § 56-1-175 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How many passengers under 21 may a special restricted license holder carry without a licensed adult 21 or older?
a: No more than two, not counting family or students going to or from school
b: No more than one, including family
exp: The limit is two passengers under 21 unless a licensed adult 21 or older rides along; family members and students going to or from school are the exceptions.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-8; S.C. Code § 56-1-180 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: When does a teen earn full driving privileges in South Carolina?
b: At 17, or after one year on a conditional or special restricted license with no offenses and no at-fault crashes
c: At 16, after six months with no tickets
d: At 17, but only after two years on a restricted license
exp: Full privileges come at 17, or after one clean year on the conditional or special restricted license.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-9; SCDMV, Teenage Drivers (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/teenage-drivers)

q: After you fail your first road test, how long must you wait to try again?
exp: The first retest comes after two business days, at any age.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-13; SCDMV, Regular License Road Test (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/testing/regular-license-road-test)

q: At what earliest age can a South Carolina teen get a conditional license?
exp: The conditional license is for teens from 15 and a half to under 16 who meet every requirement.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-7; SCDMV, Teenage Drivers (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/teenage-drivers)

q: Which license is for a driver who is at least 16 but under 17?
exp: A 16-year-old who meets the requirements, or holds a conditional license, can get a special restricted license.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-8; S.C. Code § 56-1-180 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: During daylight saving time, until what hour may a conditional license holder drive alone?
exp: The alone window runs from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., extended to 8 p.m. during daylight saving time.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-7; SCDMV, Teenage Drivers (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/teenage-drivers)

q: A 15 and a half-year-old with a conditional license wants to drive at 1 a.m. What is required?
a: Nothing, if the trip is home from work
b: Any licensed driver 18 or older must ride along
c: A qualified supervisor, such as a parent or guardian, must ride along
d: A licensed sibling must ride along
exp: From midnight to 6 a.m., a conditional or special restricted holder may drive only with a qualified supervisor listed in the law.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-8; S.C. Code § 56-1-175 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What does a special restricted license with a waiver allow a 16-year-old to do?
d: Drive alone until midnight for work or certain activities
exp: The waiver extends solo driving to midnight for work or approved activities; it never allows driving after midnight.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-9; SCDMV, Teenage Drivers (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/teenage-drivers)

q: What is the fee for a new license that adds a special restricted waiver?
exp: You pay $25 for the new license with the waiver.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-9; SCDMV, Teenage Drivers (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/teenage-drivers)

q: What does the SCDMV charge for the knowledge test?
exp: The knowledge test costs $2.00; the permit itself is $2.50 after you pass.
src: SCDMV, Beginner's Permits (dmv.sc.gov/Driver-Services/Drivers-License/Beginner-Permits)

q: What does a South Carolina beginner's permit cost?
exp: Each beginner's permit, or a renewal, costs $2.50.
src: SCDMV, Beginner's Permits (dmv.sc.gov/Driver-Services/Drivers-License/Beginner-Permits); S.C. Code § 56-1-50 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How much is an eight-year South Carolina driver's license?
exp: The SCDMV charges $25 for an eight-year license.
src: SCDMV, Moving to SC (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/moving-to-sc); South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-17

q: How long is a beginner's permit valid?
exp: A permit is issued for up to 12 months and can be renewed or replaced for further 12-month periods.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-50 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: Which of these makes you fail the knowledge test at once?
a: Using all the time you are given
b: Leaving the test area before you finish
c: Skipping a question and returning to it later
d: Wearing your glasses during the test
exp: Leaving the test area early, talking to anyone, or bringing in notes or electronic devices fails you immediately.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-10

q: To take the knowledge test at an SCDMV branch, you should arrive before what time?
exp: The SCDMV asks applicants to visit a branch before 4 p.m. for the knowledge test.
src: SCDMV, Beginner's Permits (dmv.sc.gov/Driver-Services/Drivers-License/Beginner-Permits)

q: What is South Carolina's minimum vision standard for a driver's license?
d: 20/40 in at least one eye, with lenses if needed
exp: The minimum is 20/40 corrected in one eye; lenses needed to reach it become a license restriction.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 3, p. 3-2

q: What does restriction code A on a South Carolina license mean?
a: You must wear corrective lenses when driving
b: You may drive only in daylight
c: You may drive only an automatic car
exp: Code A is the corrective lens restriction, and driving without the required lenses is illegal.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 3, pp. 3-2 to 3-3

q: How long is a Certificate of Vision Examination from an eye care professional accepted?
exp: Standard vision screening certificates are valid for 36 months.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 3, p. 3-2; South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-15

q: Which person may supervise a permit driver between midnight and 6 a.m.?
a: Any licensed friend who is 21 or older
c: Someone who has stood in place of a parent for at least 60 days
d: A neighbor 21 or older with no written permission
exp: After midnight, only a person on the qualified list may supervise, such as a parent, guardian, or a person in place of a parent for 60 days or more.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-5; S.C. Code § 56-1-50 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What is the SCDMV form PDLA?
a: The parent consent form for a permit
d: The Certification of School Attendance, Driver's Education and Driving Practice
exp: Your driver education program gives you the PDLA after you finish the course.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-7; SCDMV, Teenage Drivers (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/teenage-drivers)

q: What school rule applies to a 15 or 16-year-old applying for a first license?
a: You must be enrolled, not suspended or expelled, with satisfactory attendance
b: You must hold at least a B average
exp: Teens must be enrolled in school, including home school, and attend satisfactorily.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-6; SCDMV, Teenage Drivers (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/teenage-drivers)

q: A driver under 17 reaches 6 points within the first year on the license. What happens?
exp: Under 17, six or more points before the license is a year old brings a six-month suspension.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-8; SCDMV, Teenage Drivers (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/teenage-drivers)

q: At what point totals does the SCDMV send a 15 or 16-year-old a letter to drive more carefully?
exp: Young drivers get warning letters at 2 and at 4 points.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-19

q: How do you receive full privileges once you qualify?
a: You visit a branch for a new photo
d: The SCDMV mails a sleeve that your license must stay in
exp: No branch visit is needed; you keep your license in the mailed sleeve to use full privileges.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, pp. 1-9 to 1-10; SCDMV, Teenage Drivers (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/teenage-drivers)

q: Which mistake is an automatic fail on the South Carolina road test?
c: Adjusting your mirrors before you start
d: Asking the examiner to repeat a direction
exp: You automatically fail the skills test if you do not use your seat belt.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-12

q: How far might the examiner ask you to back up in a straight line?
exp: The skills test can include 100 feet of straight-line backing.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-12; SCDMV, Regular License Road Test (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/testing/regular-license-road-test)

q: After a second failed road test, how long must you wait?
exp: The wait is 2 business days after a first failure, 7 calendar days after a second and 30 after a third.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-13; SCDMV, Regular License Road Test (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/testing/regular-license-road-test)

q: How long must you wait after failing the road test a third time?
exp: A third or later failure means a 30-day wait, regardless of age.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-13; SCDMV, Regular License Road Test (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/testing/regular-license-road-test)

q: You want to take the road test in a rental car. What is required?
a: Your name must be on the rental contract as an insured driver
exp: The car must be properly insured; for a rental, your name must appear as an insured party on the contract.
src: SCDMV, Regular License Road Test (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/testing/regular-license-road-test)

q: You move to South Carolina for good with a valid license from another state. How long do you have to get an SC license?
exp: New residents apply within 45 days and surrender the out-of-state license.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-13; SCDMV, Moving to SC (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/moving-to-sc)

q: A new resident's out-of-state license is valid. Which test must they pass?
b: The vision, knowledge and road tests
exp: Knowledge and road tests apply only if the old license has been expired more than nine months; the vision test is always required.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-13; South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 3, p. 3-2; SCDMV, Moving to SC (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/moving-to-sc)

q: When does South Carolina waive the knowledge and road tests for a license from another country?
a: Whenever the license is written in English
b: Never; every foreign driver takes all tests
c: When the driver also holds an International Driving Permit
d: When the country has a formal reciprocity agreement with SC and the license is not expired more than nine months
exp: Only a license from a reciprocity country, not expired more than nine months, skips the knowledge and skills tests.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, pp. 1-14 to 1-15

q: At an SCDMV branch, when must you have an appointment for a regular road test?
exp: Walk-ins are taken in the morning and early afternoon; tests from 2 to 4 p.m. need an appointment.
src: SCDMV, Regular License Road Test (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/testing/regular-license-road-test)

q: How many proofs of address does a REAL ID card require?
exp: A REAL ID needs two proofs of your current physical address.
src: SCDMV, Beginner's Permits (dmv.sc.gov/Driver-Services/Drivers-License/Beginner-Permits); SCDMV, Moving to SC (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/moving-to-sc)

q: How does a permit applicant under 18 get parental consent?
a: A notarized letter mailed in later is enough
b: A school teacher signs the form
c: A qualified adult signs at the branch and shows a photo ID
exp: The authorized adult signs at an SCDMV branch, unless a driver training school submits the consent.
src: SCDMV, Beginner's Permits (dmv.sc.gov/Driver-Services/Drivers-License/Beginner-Permits)

q: What is an International Driving Permit?
a: A license that replaces your foreign license
b: A permit every U.S. visitor must buy
d: A translation of your foreign license, carried with it
exp: It translates a foreign license into English for police; it is not a license by itself.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-14

q: In a South Carolina work zone, what is the fine for endangering a highway worker when no one is hurt?
exp: Endangerment of a highway worker with no injury costs $500 to $1,000, and the fine cannot be reduced.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1535 (2025 code, law.justia.com); S.C. Code § 56-5-1535 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: How many points does endangering a highway worker add when no one is injured?
exp: The offense costs 2 points, or 4 if a worker is injured.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-720 (2025 code, law.justia.com); S.C. Code § 56-5-1535 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: What is the speed limit in a South Carolina school zone?
c: The limit posted for that zone, when its lights flash or posted hours apply
exp: State law sets no single school zone speed; each zone's sign gives the limit and when it applies.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1520 (2025 code, law.justia.com); South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 6, p. 6-4

q: Which act counts as endangering a highway worker in South Carolina?
a: Driving the posted work zone speed
b: Merging early when a lane closes
c: Turning on your headlights in a work zone
d: Driving through a work zone in a lane you are not allowed to use
exp: Using an unauthorized lane or ignoring work zone signs, cones or flaggers is endangerment of a highway worker.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1535 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: If a highway worker is injured because you ignored work zone controls, how many points are added?
exp: Endangerment that injures a worker adds 4 points.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-720 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What color are many South Carolina school zone and school crossing signs?
exp: Some warning signs, such as school zones and school crossings, are fluorescent yellow-green.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 6, p. 6-4

q: Can a judge lower the fine for endangering a highway worker below the minimum?
b: Yes, if no workers were present
exp: The law makes the fine mandatory; it may not be waived or reduced below the minimum.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1535 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: In South Carolina, when may you turn right on a steady red light?
a: After a full stop, unless a sign forbids it
b: Without stopping, if no one is coming
c: Only when a green arrow is also lit
d: Never; right on red is not allowed
exp: After stopping, you may turn right on red unless a sign prohibits it, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 6, p. 6-3; S.C. Code § 56-5-970 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: When may you turn left on a steady red light in South Carolina?
a: After a full stop, from any left turn lane
b: After a full stop, from a one-way street onto another one-way street
c: Only with a police officer's signal
exp: Left on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street, after a stop.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-970 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: You face a steady red arrow pointing right. What must you do?
a: Stop, then turn right when clear
b: Slow down and turn if no one is coming
c: Stay stopped; you may not make that turn until a green signal allows it
exp: Traffic facing a steady red arrow may not enter the intersection to make that movement.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-970 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: Before turning right on red, where must you stop?
a: In the middle of the crosswalk
b: Past the stop line, at the curb
c: Only where you can see the signal
d: Before the crosswalk on the near side of the turn
exp: Stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side, then yield to pedestrians and other traffic.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 6, p. 6-3

q: A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on a two-lane road, and you are coming toward it. What must you do?
c: Continue; only traffic behind the bus stops
d: Stop only if children are in the road
exp: On a two-lane road, drivers from both directions stop for a bus with flashing red lights.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2770 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: On a highway with four or more lanes, at least two each way, a school bus stops with red lights flashing. You are coming from the opposite direction. What must you do?
b: You need not stop, but watch for children
d: Stop until the driver waves you on
exp: On a multilane highway with two or more lanes each way, oncoming traffic need not stop; traffic behind the bus must.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2770 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: On a two-lane road, an ambulance with siren and flashing lights comes up behind you. What must you do?
a: Speed up to clear the way
b: Stop right where you are in your lane
c: Pull as close as possible to the right edge or curb and stop until it passes
exp: On a two-lane road you move to the right edge or curb and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2360 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How many points does passing a stopped school bus add to your record?
exp: Passing a stopped school bus is a 6-point violation.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-720 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What is the penalty for a first offense of passing a stopped school bus?
a: A fine of at least $500 or up to 30 days in jail
exp: A first offense brings a fine of at least $500 or up to 30 days in jail.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2780 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: A school bus ahead of you shows flashing amber lights. What does South Carolina law say?
a: Pass it quickly before the lights turn red
c: Amber lights apply only to oncoming traffic
exp: No driver may overtake a school bus showing its amber signals.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2770 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: After stopping for a school bus with flashing red lights, when may you go?
b: When the stop arm is half folded
c: When the bus moves again or the red lights go off
d: When the first child reaches the sidewalk
exp: You may not proceed until the bus resumes motion or the red lights stop flashing.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2770 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What is the fine for violating South Carolina's Move Over law?
exp: Endangering emergency personnel by failing to slow and move over is punished by a $300 to $500 fine.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1538 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: You approach a stopped police car with blue lights flashing on a road with two lanes going your way. What should you do?
a: Slow down a lot and move to the lane not next to it, if safe
b: Keep your speed and stay in your lane
c: Stop in your lane until it leaves
d: Speed up to pass it quickly
exp: Slow significantly and change to a lane not adjacent to the stopped vehicle if it is safe; otherwise keep a safe, slower speed.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1538 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: Does South Carolina's Move Over law cover a car stopped on the shoulder with its hazard lights on?
a: No; it covers only police cars
b: Yes; slow down and move over if you safely can
c: No; it covers only tow trucks
exp: The law also applies to a stopped vehicle displaying flashing hazard lights.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1538 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: On a multilane road, a fire truck with siren and lights approaches. What does South Carolina law require?
a: Always stop in the left lane
b: Speed up to the next exit
c: Stay in or move to a spot that lets it pass safely
exp: On multilane roads you yield by staying in or moving to a position that lets the emergency vehicle pass safely.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2360 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How far before a turn does South Carolina law require you to signal?
exp: The signal must be given continuously for at least the last 100 feet before turning.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2150 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: You may not make a U-turn on a curve or near a hilltop where other drivers cannot see your car within how many feet?
exp: U-turns are banned where a driver from either direction could not see you within 500 feet.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2140 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: When is a U-turn legal in South Carolina, where no sign forbids it?
c: When you can make it safely without interfering with other traffic
exp: You may turn around only if it can be done safely and without interfering with other traffic.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2140 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: Can you use a hand and arm signal instead of your signal lights in South Carolina?
exp: South Carolina allows either hand and arm signals or signal lamps.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2150 (2025 code, law.justia.com); S.C. Code § 56-5-2180 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What is the maximum speed in a South Carolina urban district when no sign is posted?
exp: Thirty miles an hour is the maximum speed in an urban district unless posted otherwise.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1520 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: What is the highest speed limit that may be posted on a South Carolina interstate?
exp: Interstates and other freeways may be posted at 70 mph.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1520 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: What minimum following distance does the South Carolina manual teach?
exp: The manual teaches at least four seconds behind the vehicle ahead, and more in bad conditions.
src: South Carolina Driver's Manual, earlier SCDMV edition (scdps.sc.gov copy), Sec. 8

q: Where no other limit is posted, what is the speed limit on a South Carolina road outside an urban district?
exp: The default limit in other locations is 55 mph.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1520 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: What is the speed limit on an unpaved South Carolina road?
exp: Unpaved roads are limited to 40 mph.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1520 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: What speed may be posted on a multilane divided primary highway in South Carolina?
exp: Multilane divided primary highways may be posted at 60 mph.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1520 (scstatehouse.gov)

q: How many points does speeding 10 mph or less over the limit cost?
exp: Speeding no more than 10 mph over is 2 points.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-720 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How many points does speeding 25 mph or more over the limit cost?
exp: Speeding 25 mph or more over the limit is 6 points.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-720 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How many points does speeding more than 10 but less than 25 mph over the limit cost?
exp: That middle range of speeding is 4 points.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-720 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How many points does following too closely cost in South Carolina?
exp: Following too closely is a 4-point violation.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-720 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in South Carolina?
exp: Standing or parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is banned.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2530 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: When you park at a curb in South Carolina, how far from it may your wheels be?
exp: Park with your wheels no more than 18 inches from the curb.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2560 (2025 code, law.justia.com); South Carolina Driver's Manual, earlier SCDMV edition (scdps.sc.gov copy), Sec. 8

q: How close to the nearest rail of a railroad crossing may you park?
exp: Parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing is banned.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2530 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How close to a crosswalk at an intersection may you park?
exp: You may not stand or park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2530 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How close to a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal at the side of the road may you park?
exp: Standing or parking within 30 feet of the approach to those devices is banned.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2530 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How close to a fire station driveway on the same side of the street may you park?
exp: Stay at least 20 feet from a fire station driveway entrance.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2530 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: Where signs are posted, how far from a fire station entrance must you stay when parking across the street?
exp: On the opposite side of the street, the limit is 75 feet when properly signposted.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2530 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: Where may you never stop in South Carolina, even for a moment?
b: At a curb more than 30 feet from a stop sign
d: On a controlled-access highway, except in an emergency
exp: Stopping is banned on controlled-access highways, sidewalks, crosswalks, bridges and railroad tracks, except to avoid conflict or obey police.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2530 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How much space does South Carolina law require when you pass a bicycle?
a: A safe operating distance at all times; the law sets no number in feet
exp: Drivers must keep a safe operating distance from a bicycle at all times; the statute gives no fixed distance.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-3435 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: You want to pass a cyclist in a narrow lane. What should you do first?
a: Honk so the cyclist moves over
b: Wait until the opposite lane is clear
c: Pass with a few inches to spare
d: Follow closely until a gap appears
exp: Wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass slowly with as much room as you can give.
src: South Carolina Driver's Manual, earlier SCDMV edition (scdps.sc.gov copy), Sec. 8

q: In which direction must cyclists ride in South Carolina?
c: With traffic, in the same direction as cars
exp: Cyclists ride in the same direction as other traffic.
src: South Carolina Driver's Manual, earlier SCDMV edition (scdps.sc.gov copy), Sec. 8

q: When must your headlights be on in South Carolina?
a: From a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise
c: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
exp: Lights are required from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, and at other times listed in the law.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-4450 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How close to an oncoming vehicle must you be before switching to low beams?
exp: Within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle, aim your lights so the glare does not reach the other driver.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-4780 (2025 code, law.justia.com); South Carolina Driver's Manual, earlier SCDMV edition (scdps.sc.gov copy), Sec. 8

q: In bad weather, South Carolina requires headlights when you cannot clearly see people and vehicles how far ahead?
exp: Headlights are required when conditions keep you from clearly seeing persons and vehicles 500 feet ahead.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-4450 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: When following another vehicle, within what distance must you use low beams?
exp: Do not use high beams within 200 feet of a vehicle you are following, unless passing.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-4780 (2025 code, law.justia.com); South Carolina Driver's Manual, earlier SCDMV edition (scdps.sc.gov copy), Sec. 8

q: It is noon, and steady rain has your wipers running. What does South Carolina law require?
exp: Headlights are required whenever wipers are in use because of rain, sleet or snow.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-4450 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What is the fine for not using headlights when South Carolina law requires them?
exp: A violation of the headlight law is a misdemeanor with a fine of up to $25.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-4450 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How many points does failing to dim your lights cost?
exp: Failing to dim lights is a 2-point violation.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-720 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: No officer investigated your crash, which caused $1,500 in damage. What must you do?
a: Nothing, since no one was hurt
d: Send a written report to the SCDMV within 15 days
exp: When no officer investigates a crash with injury, death or $1,000 or more in damage, the driver or owner reports within 15 days.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1270 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: You are in a crash with an injury inside a city. Whom must you notify at once?
exp: Inside a municipality, notify local police; outside one, the sheriff or Highway Patrol.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-1260 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What color lights does a South Carolina police car use to signal you to stop?
exp: In South Carolina, only emergency vehicles may display blue or red lights, and police signal with blue lights.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-170 (scstatehouse.gov); South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-22

q: What is the penalty for a first offense of failing to stop for a police signal, with no one hurt?
c: At least a $500 fine and a license suspension of at least 30 days
exp: A first offense is a misdemeanor with a fine of at least $500 and at least a 30-day suspension.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-750 (scstatehouse.gov); Act No. 38 of 2025 (H.3127)

q: Which documents must you carry every time you drive in South Carolina?
d: Your license, vehicle registration and insurance card
exp: Drivers must have a valid license, registration and insurance card in their possession.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-3

q: At what alcohol concentration is a South Carolina driver under 21 in violation of the law?
exp: Drivers under 21 with 0.02 percent or more face suspension.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 3, p. 3-7; S.C. Code § 56-1-286 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How long is the suspension for a first refusal to take a test for alcohol in South Carolina?
exp: A first refusal brings a six-month suspension.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2951 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What is the fine for a first violation of South Carolina's hands-free law?
exp: A first offense costs $100; a second within three years costs $200 and 2 points.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 3, p. 3-5; S.C. Code § 56-5-3890 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What is DUAC in South Carolina?
a: Driving with any drug in your system
d: Driving with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more
exp: DUAC means driving with an unlawful alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 3, p. 3-7; S.C. Code § 56-5-2933 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What happens on a first offense if a driver's test shows 0.15 percent or more?
exp: A first test of 0.15 or more brings a one-month administrative suspension.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2951 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How long is the suspension for a second refusal of a chemical test?
exp: Refusal suspensions grow from 6 months to 9, 12 and 15 months with prior offenses.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2951 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: After a suspension notice for refusing a test, how long do you have to request a hearing?
exp: You may request a contested case hearing within 30 days of the notice.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2951 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What does a temporary alcohol license cost while your hearing is pending?
exp: The SCDMV issues a temporary alcohol license for $100 pending the hearing.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-23; S.C. Code § 56-5-2951 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What is the fine for a first DUI with a BAC under 0.10?
a: $400, or 48 hours to 30 days in jail
d: $500, or 72 hours to 30 days in jail
exp: The lowest tier for a first offense is a $400 fine or 48 hours to 30 days in jail.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2930 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: A first DUI with a BAC of 0.16 or more brings what jail range, if jail is imposed?
exp: At 0.16 or more, a first offense brings a $1,000 fine or 30 to 90 days in jail.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2930 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: After a first DUI conviction, what must you use to drive again?
a: A route-restricted license for one year
c: An ignition interlock device for six months
exp: A first offense requires the Ignition Interlock Device Program, with the device installed for six months.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-2990 (2025 code, law.justia.com); South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-21

q: Where may an opened bottle of wine ride in a car on a South Carolina highway?
a: In the cup holder, if the driver is sober
c: On the back seat, if it is corked
d: In the trunk or luggage compartment
exp: Open beer or wine is allowed only in the trunk or luggage compartment.
src: S.C. Code § 61-4-110 (2025 code, law.justia.com); S.C. Code § 61-6-4020 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What is the maximum fine for an open container of beer or wine in a vehicle?
exp: The open container offense brings a fine of up to $100 or up to 30 days in jail.
src: S.C. Code § 61-4-110 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How long is a first suspension for a driver under 21 who tests at 0.02 percent or more?
exp: The first suspension is three months, or six with a qualifying prior within three years.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 3, p. 3-7; S.C. Code § 56-1-286 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: A driver under 21 refuses an alcohol test. How long is the first suspension?
exp: Under 21, a first refusal brings at least six months.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 3, p. 3-7; S.C. Code § 56-1-286 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What is the fine for a person under 21 who buys or possesses alcohol?
d: $100 to $200, or up to 30 days in jail
exp: The misdemeanor costs $100 to $200 or up to 30 days, plus an alcohol education program.
src: S.C. Code § 63-19-2450 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: A 19-year-old is convicted of possessing alcohol. How long is the first license suspension?
exp: Convictions for underage alcohol possession or purchase bring a 120-day suspension, one year for a repeat.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-746 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What penalty applies to a second hands-free violation within three years?
exp: A second or later offense within three years costs $200 and 2 points.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 3, p. 3-5; S.C. Code § 56-5-3890 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: Under South Carolina's hands-free law, which is allowed while driving?
a: Holding the phone to read a map
b: Typing a short text at low speed
c: Talking through an earpiece without holding the phone
d: Watching a video on a mounted phone
exp: Earpieces and wrist devices for voice calls are allowed; holding the phone, texting and watching video are not.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 3, p. 3-5; S.C. Code § 56-5-3890 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What are South Carolina's minimum liability insurance limits?
a: $25,000 per person and $50,000 per crash for injury, $25,000 property damage
exp: The minimums are 25/50/25.
src: S.C. Code § 38-77-140 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What kind of seat belt law does South Carolina have?
b: Primary: police may stop you for a seat belt violation alone
d: Belts are required only for drivers under 18
exp: Officers may stop a driver after a clear view of an unbelted driver or occupant.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 4, p. 4-6

q: How must a child under 2 ride in South Carolina?
a: In a forward-facing seat in the front
c: In a rear-facing car seat in a rear seat
d: On an adult's lap with a belt
exp: Under 2, a child rides rear-facing in a rear seat until outgrowing the seat's limits.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 4, p. 4-7; S.C. Code § 56-5-6410 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: What is the fine for a South Carolina seat belt violation?
exp: The fine is up to $25, and the violation is not added to your driving record.
src: S.C. Code § 56-5-6540 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: At what age may a child who has outgrown a forward-facing seat move to a booster?
exp: From age 4, a child who outgrew the forward-facing seat rides in a booster in a rear seat.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 4, p. 4-7; S.C. Code § 56-5-6410 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: When may a child use an adult seat belt in South Carolina?
b: At age 8, or at 57 inches tall, if the belt fits properly
exp: A child at least 8 or 57 inches tall may use an adult belt if it fits properly.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 4, p. 4-7; S.C. Code § 56-5-6410 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How do points on a South Carolina record change after one year?
d: They stay the same for five years
exp: Points are reduced by half one year after the violation date.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-18

q: How many points trigger a license suspension for a driver 17 or older?
exp: At 12 points the license is suspended; 6 points bring a warning letter.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-19; S.C. Code § 56-1-740 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How long is the suspension for 12 to 15 points?
exp: 12 to 15 points bring three months, rising to six months at 20 or more.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-740 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: How many points can a defensive driving course remove, and how often?
a: Up to 2 points, once a year
b: Up to 4 points, once every three years
c: All points, once in a lifetime
d: Up to 6 points, every two years
exp: An approved 8-hour classroom course taken in South Carolina reduces points once in a three-year period.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, pp. 1-19 to 1-20

q: What does it cost to clear a suspension for driving your own car uninsured?
c: A $700 fee, plus an SR-22 filing for three years
exp: The license and registration stay suspended until a $700 uninsured motorist fee is paid and an SR-22 is filed for three years.
src: SCDMV, Facts About Driving Uninsured (dmv.sc.gov)

q: At how many points does a driver 17 or older get a warning letter?
exp: Drivers 17 and older get a letter at 6 points; suspension comes at 12.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-19

q: A load in your truck bed could slide or blow off. What does South Carolina law say?
a: Driving with an unsecured load is a crime
b: It is legal if you drive slowly
c: It is legal on local roads
d: It applies only to commercial trucks
exp: A driver who fails to secure a load is guilty of a misdemeanor and may pay cleanup costs.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 4, p. 4-8

q: How long is the suspension for 20 or more points?
exp: Suspension length rises with points, reaching six months at 20 or more.
src: S.C. Code § 56-1-740 (2025 code, law.justia.com)

q: Which feature are you not allowed to use during the South Carolina road test?
exp: Safety features such as parking assist and cruise control are not allowed during the driving test.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 4, p. 4-9

q: Which of these may be part of the South Carolina road test?
exp: The skills test can include parallel parking, parking on a hill, backing, turnabouts and interstate driving.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-12; SCDMV, Regular License Road Test (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/testing/regular-license-road-test)

q: Who may be in or around the car during your South Carolina road test?
a: You, the examiner and your parent
c: Only you and the SCDMV examiner
d: Your driving instructor in the back seat
exp: You and the SCDMV employee are the only people allowed in or around the vehicle.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-12

q: Your car's defroster does not work on test day. What happens?
c: The examiner lends you a car
d: The test is postponed until the car is safe
exp: The defroster is on the required list, and the test is postponed if the vehicle is not safe.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-12; SCDMV, Regular License Road Test (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/testing/regular-license-road-test)

q: Which turnabout might you be asked to perform on the South Carolina road test?
d: A turn on a red arrow
exp: The test may include reverse and forward two-point turnabouts and a three-point turnabout.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, pp. 1-12 to 1-13

q: Can the SCDMV ask you to retake the road test after you pass?
b: Yes, it may pick you at random before issuing your license
d: Only if you had a ticket
exp: The SCDMV may randomly select applicants to pass the skills test again before a license is issued.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-11

q: You have failed the South Carolina road test twice. What is the soonest you may test again?
exp: The waits are 2 business days after a first failure, 7 calendar days after a second and 30 days after a third or later.
src: South Carolina Driver's License Manual (SCDMV), Sec. 1, p. 1-13; SCDMV, Regular License Road Test (dmv.sc.gov/driver-services/drivers-license/testing/regular-license-road-test)
